extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers and benchmark designers evaluating LLM mathematical reasoning
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running evaluations of large language models as grade-school mathematical problem solvers (variants of GSM8K), including dataset variants, prompting, decoding, statistical testing, and analyses of robustness and failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributional evaluation over multiple instantiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess performance across many different instantiations of the same question rather than relying on a single-point accuracy metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper stresses that single-point accuracy is unreliable: measure performance variability (e.g., run 50 different templates/instantiations) and report distributions (means, standard deviations) to capture sensitivity to phrasing/templating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to inconsequential (No-Op) information
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether models ignore seemingly relevant but operationally inconsequential statements (No-Op) added to problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GSM-NoOp was introduced to test this; large drops in accuracy on GSM-NoOp indicate models convert statements to operations without understanding (e.g., treating a 'discount' mention as multiplication regardless of context). Report accuracy drop relative to baseline (GSM8K→GSM-NoOp accuracy drop %).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to numerical value changes vs proper names
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how model performance changes when question numerical values change versus when proper names or surface tokens change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors observed LLMs are relatively robust to changes in proper names but more sensitive to variations in numerical values; include tests that isolate these factors when constructing variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to question difficulty / complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how model accuracy and variance change as question difficulty increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance tends to deteriorate and variance increases with higher difficulty; include difficulty-graded variants (e.g., GSM-P1 vs GSM-P2) and report trends and per-difficulty distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of few-shot chain-of-thought (8-shot CoT) prompting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use chain-of-thought prompting with eight demonstration shots to probe reasoning; evaluate whether CoT shots recover performance across variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses an 8-shot CoT prompt template for evaluations; authors found that providing reasoning-chain shots (NoOp-Symb — 8 shots of the same question from GSM-Symbolic) did not recover performance on GSM-NoOp, indicating CoT shots may not fix spurious reasoning behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of shot source and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Test different sources of in-context shots (original GSM8K, GSM-Symbolic, GSM-NoOp shots of same/different questions) to see how shot choice influences target accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They evaluate NoOp-Symb (shots are GSM-Symbolic variants of the same question) and NoOp-NoOp (shots are GSM-NoOp from different questions). Despite using exact-question symbolic shots, performance on NoOp variants remained within standard deviation; document shot provenance and expected/observed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt format and explicit reply structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify and use a consistent prompt template that includes a preamble system instruction and shot Q/A format with 'Let's think step by step.' for chain-of-thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt format used: preamble ('As an expert problem solver, solve step by step the following mathematical questions.'), then 8 Q/A shots with 'Let’s think step by step. {{solution}}. The final answer is {{final answer}}.' and the target question followed by 'Let’s think step by step.'; report exact prompt used for reproducibility (Figure 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoding strategy control and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Control and report the decoding method used when generating model responses (greedy, sampling, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reported evaluations use greedy decoding except when API constraints prevent controlling decoding (noted for o1-mini and o1-preview); explicitly state exceptions and that some APIs returned non-deterministic outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation stopping criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Define when model generation is considered finished during evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop generation when context size limit is reached, when an end-of-response token (e.g., '</s>' or '<|endoftext|>') is generated, or when the model finishes answering the current question and moves on (indicated by generation of another 'Q:').

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting metrics: accuracy, mean/std, and accuracy drop
rubrics_metrics.description: Report main metrics such as accuracy on full test sets and subsets, distributional statistics (mean and standard deviation), and relative drops (e.g., GSM8K→GSM-NoOp accuracy drop %).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both full-test accuracy (e.g., GSM8K full set) and subset accuracy (e.g., 100-question subset used to make templates), plus distribution plots and tables (Table 1, Figures 8–12) and ± standard deviations for distributional runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical testing and choice of test
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and report statistical tests for significance with clear assumptions and alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors used one-sample t-test (two-sided) to test whether 50 GSM-Symbolic scores differ from the original 100-question GSM8K mean, verified normality of distributions (skewness/kurtosis test, p=0.1), but note criticisms (Ivanova et al.) that a two-sample z-test may be more appropriate; explicitly state assumptions (i.i.d., normality) and sensitivity of conclusions to test choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset variant construction and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct and document dataset variants (GSM-Symbolic, GSM-NoOp, GSM-P1, GSM-P2, Symbolic-M1/P1/P2/NoOp) that target specific perturbations (symbolic replacements, No-Op additions, difficulty changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide descriptions of each variant and how templates are derived (e.g., adding No-Op clauses to GSM-Symbolic templates to form GSM-NoOp), include the number of templates/samples, and share examples and failure cases in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation: effect of fine-tuning on easier tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether fine-tuning on easier variants improves performance on harder variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors show finetuning Phi-3.5 on GSM-P1 slightly improves P1 but decreases performance on GSM-P2; include controlled finetuning experiments (e.g., 10k generated examples from 50 templates) and report epoch/shot details and cross-task transfer effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect qualitative failure modes and exemplar outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and present failure cases and example model outputs to illustrate error modes (e.g., naive application of inflation, misapplied operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples like o1-preview applying 10% inflation incorrectly because it treated the phrase as operationally relevant; show step-by-step model outputs to reveal pattern-matching behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation criterion: distinguishing genuine reasoning vs pattern matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Use behavioral evidence (high variance across instantiations, sensitivity to No-Op info, common mis-conversions) to judge whether model performance reflects genuine mathematical reasoning or sophisticated pattern matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors argue that large variance, catastrophic drops with inconsequential info, and consistent mistaken operation conversions (e.g., 'discount'→multiplication) indicate fragile, pattern-matching-like reasoning rather than robust logical reasoning; use this as a qualitative evaluation axis.
